author: WP07
summary: Separates CNA's four shader routes — renderer-owned stock semantics, DIRECTX9 recompilation of Microsoft's stock sources (61/66 bytecode match), compiled Effect Framework bytecode, and the renderer-specific ShaderEffect — and gives the ShaderEffect object contract, its 3D path and arbitrary-layout fix. Partly stale at TARGET: nine (not eight) opt-in compiled-effect families, WebGPU, Vulkan, SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11/12 now consume ShaderEffect in 3D draws with reflection-based uniforms, diagnostics accessors exist and disposal releases the program. The site's Shader Effects and Effects System pages had the usage and per-renderer input table; the route comparison, compiled-effect internals and object contract went into two new deep dives with the figure recreated.

concepts.text: CNA has no single answer to XNA effects but four separate shader-delivery strategies: CNA-owned stock semantics, DIRECTX9 recompilation of Microsoft's stock sources, compiled Effect Framework bytecode on qualified renderers, and the renderer-specific ShaderEffect.
Formats that share a 'compiled shader' description (Effect Framework binaries, DXBC, MGFX, SPIR-V) are not interchangeable; support for one route never implies another.
tokens: Support for one route never implies another

target.evidence: Effect.cpp (structural check, MGFX refusal); GraphicsCapability.hpp (CompiledEffects vs CustomEffects)

concepts.text: CNAEXT engine-layer passes form a further route: they select a variant from multi-language shader packages (GLSL ES, GLSL 330, SPIR-V, WGSL) on renderers that accept one of those languages.

A normal XNA game ships no .fx source: the content pipeline compiles .fx at build time to Direct3D 9 Effect Framework bytecode stored in .xnb, loaded at run time through new Effect(GraphicsDevice, byte[]) or ContentManager.Load<Effect>.

FNA ships MojoShader, a parser and cross-compiler that turns Direct3D 9 shader bytecode into GLSL or other targets at load time, which lets FNA run XNA effect content without source; CNA uses a pinned MojoShader through the FNA3D checkout.
For a port, inventory each asset loaded through the general EffectReader and each direct bytecode-constructor call — those are what the compiled route must accept.

Two public entry points share one route: the Effect byte constructor (validate container, check CompiledEffects, create runtime, build reflected graph) and the general XNB EffectReader, which reads a length-prefixed payload and calls the same constructor.
EffectReader wraps constructor and backend failures (including an incapable renderer's NotSupportedException) in ContentLoadException naming the asset; it is not a permanent refusal reader.
tokens: could not create the compiled effect

concepts.text: EffectReader refuses a negative length or one above 64 MiB and requires a ContentManager with a graphics device; the effect is named after the asset.
tokens: names the effect after the asset

concepts.text: The route reflects parameters, arrays, structures, annotations, techniques and passes with the binary's own names.

EffectPass::Apply() on a compiled effect uploads dirty parameters, selects technique and pass, applies native state and makes the effect current for SpriteBatch or 3D draws on an implementing renderer.
Pass render and sampler state is published back through the device's own state objects and sampler/texture collections, so a game observes it as if it had assigned it (XNA/FNA behaviour).
tokens: exactly as if it had assigned it

concepts.text: Clone() duplicates the native runtime, parameter values and current-technique choice while keeping resources on the same graphics device.
Admission is narrow: an Effect Framework container (including the XNA 4 wrapper form), at most 64 MiB, with bounded reflection and object graphs.

The preflight bounds: at least one and at most 4,096 techniques, at most 16,384 parameters and 65,536 objects, nesting below 32 levels, every offset inside the buffer, because the pinned MojoShader parser trusts relative offsets.
Malformed input is judged before the renderer is consulted, so the same bad bytes give the same ArgumentException on every renderer; only a valid binary reaches the capability check.
tokens: Malformed input is judged before the renderer is consulted

concepts.text: .fx source, HLSL text, raw DXBC and the MonoGame MGFX container are different inputs and are refused; MGFX is recognised by its magic and refused by name.

The feature needs both a parser and a renderer runtime; metadata parsing alone never promotes the capability, and CompiledEffects is derived from SupportsCompiledEffects() rather than a renderer's permissive switch.
tokens: A parser alone never enables the capability

concepts.section: Answer one: reimplement the stock semantics
concepts.text: Most renderers never consume XNA bytecode for stock effects: the five public stock effects translate properties into GpuDrawParams and each renderer selects CNA-authored shader variants for fog, vertex colour, alpha test and lighting combinations.

concepts.section: Answer three: execute compiled Effect Framework bytecode
concepts.text: FNA3D is the always-on compiled-effect implementation and the provenance of CNA's six FNA-derived stock .fxb files (106,700 bytes together), committed with a CNA conformance effect beside them.

concepts.section: Answer three: execute compiled Effect Framework bytecode
concepts.text: Each family registers a conformance test on the shared gate CompiledEffectConformance.hpp; the option-gated families are not built by a default configure.
ShaderEffect presents one constructor shape and one IEffectRenderer contract to every renderer, but the strings are not a portable format — each renderer decides what they mean.
A renderer returning an effect object proves only that an object exists, not that arbitrary source compiles, every setter has meaning or a 3D draw consumes the program.
tokens: proves only that an object exists

concepts.text: EasyGL compiles GLSL through the driver; SpriteBatch and general 3D draws consume it, uniform names and array setters are real, and 2D, cube and volume texture binds each have a pixel test.
tokens: uniform names and array setters are real

concepts.text: SDL_GPU accepts SPIR-V words whenever a device exists and compiles GLSL through libshaderc only where the build found it; SpriteBatch (including a two-output MRT shader) and 3D draws consume it — the chapter's '32-byte vertex / 128-byte uniform, SpriteBatch only' description is stale.
concepts.note: Corrected: SPIR-V intake and 3D consumption at TARGET.

concepts.text: VULKAN's two strings carry raw precompiled SPIR-V bytes (size a multiple of four), not GLSL; SpriteBatch (Vulkan_ShaderEffect_SpirV) and 3D draws via QueueCustomEffect3DDrawEXT consume them.
concepts.note: Corrected: the chapter limits Vulkan to SpriteBatch.

concepts.text: DIRECTX9 compiles HLSL at run time for SM2 (SM3 under HiDef) and consumes it in SpriteBatch only, with a colour-inversion pixel test.

DIRECTX11/12 compile HLSL as vs_5_0/ps_5_0; at TARGET named setters reach constant-buffer members through shader reflection and 3D draws consume the program when its vertex signature matches the bound declaration — the chapter's 'setter names ignored, SpriteBatch facility' is stale.
concepts.note: Corrected: reflection-based uniforms and 3D paths exist.

concepts.text: SDL_RENDERER has no effect renderer: construction leaves IsEffectValid() false and passing the effect to SpriteBatch::Begin throws std::runtime_error, while merely constructing it does not.
tokens: no programmable shader stage exists on this renderer

concepts.text: The chapter says WebGPU and FREEDIRECT inherit a null CreateEffectRenderer; at TARGET WEBGPU compiles WGSL for SpriteBatch and 3D draws, while FREEDIRECT and CANVAS reject a custom SpriteBatch effect.
concepts.note: Corrected: WebGPU now has a source route.

concepts.text: SOFTWARE accepts any non-empty pair and keeps rendering through its fixed CPU path; HEADLESS records compilation, binds and uniforms without shader pixels — test contracts, not custom-shader support.
METAL throws NotSupportedException from CreateEffectRenderer and refuses custom-effect 3D draws until adapted macOS evidence exists.
FNA3D and PORTABLEGL have no effect renderer; PORTABLEGL refuses a custom-program 3D draw by name.

concepts.text: IEffectRenderer's default setters are empty no-ops, so a SetUniformXxx() can be structurally accepted without changing GPU state unless the concrete renderer overrides it.
ShaderEffect's device queries — GetShaderDialectEXT(), SupportsShaderLanguageEXT(), ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() — let an application ask the live renderer which payload it wants.
The ShaderEffect header's class comment still calls it a 'GLSL-source-based effect'; that is stale cross-renderer documentation, not an enforced constraint.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: The ShaderEffect constructor copies both source strings, so construction from temporaries or later-modified strings is safe.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: If the device has a renderer the constructor asks it once for an IEffectRenderer; an invalid program writes the compiler log to standard error and the constructor continues.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: A null program and a failed compile both leave IsEffectValid() false; HasRenderer() distinguishes them, and GetCompileErrorEXT()/GetShaderDiagnosticsEXT() give the reason — the chapter's 'no public accessor for the diagnostic' is stale.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: The no-throw design is deliberate: on several renderers CustomEffects is true while text is never compiled, and throwing would turn a capability boundary into a crash; a renderer may still throw from its own factory.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: Validity is a precondition: Effect::Apply() rejects a disposed effect, ShaderEffect::OnApply() binds a valid program or only logs a debug message, and applying an invalid effect still replaces the device's current effect.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: There is no automatic retry or recompilation; construct a new effect after correcting source or changing renderer.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: Uniform and texture calls are immediate submissions: ShaderEffect keeps no uniform dictionary, sampler table or texture ownership; SetUniformXxx forwards name and value and SetTexture forwards the texture renderer's address.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: The common layer checks no uniform name, sampler-unit range, array count or pointer; renderers upload at the call, stage into a block, do nothing (interface defaults) or record for tracing.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: A successful setter call is not a portable binding guarantee and never transfers texture ownership; keep textures alive through their owner and rebind when the path requires.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: The setters do not inspect IsDisposed; the chapter says they keep forwarding while the renderer object lives, but at TARGET Dispose() releases the program so later setters are silent no-ops.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: ShaderEffect::Clone() builds new ShaderEffect(device, vertexSource, fragmentSource): an independent program, identity matrices, copied diagnostic labels and selected language; no uniforms, texture binds, metadata or program handle.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: The header explains why the program is not shared: the effect uniquely owns its renderer program and sharing would need reference-counted ownership.

concepts.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
concepts.text: Unlike the stock effects' Clone(), ShaderEffect::Clone() does not check whether the source has been disposed.

concepts.section: A minimal GLSL ShaderEffect adapted from a test
concepts.text: A minimal cube-map shader (samplerCube uniform bound to unit 0, direction uniform) adapted from easygl_shadereffect_texturecube_test.cpp; GLSL ES 3.00 compiles only on OPENGLES3 and WEBGL2.

concepts.section: A minimal GLSL ShaderEffect adapted from a test
concepts.text: Check IsEffectValid() before drawing: a syntax error or unsupported feature in game-supplied source yields an invalid effect that must be reported before submission.
There is no HLSL-specific overload: on a Direct3D renderer the same two-string constructor compiles HLSL.
The DIRECTX9 SpriteBatch sets a vpSize uniform from the current viewport so a custom vertex shader can map SpriteBatch's pixel-space positions to normalised device coordinates.
The source test also samples outside the destination rectangle and expects the clear colour, proving the NDC mapping rather than a full-screen paint.

For a long stretch a ShaderEffect applied before DrawIndexedPrimitives (the ModelMesh::Draw shape) was silently ignored: it lacked IEffectMatrices, its FillGpuDrawParams was the base no-op and EasyGL fell back to a stride-selected stock shader.

The fix: GpuDrawParams gained customEffectRenderer, ShaderEffect implements IEffectMatrices so ExtractMatrices reads its World/View/Projection, and the draw binds the custom program and those uniforms instead of a stock shader.
The uniform names World, View and Projection match the names XNA samples' own .fx sources use.
easygl_shadereffect_3d_test.cpp draws a quad twice with an N·L shader: World = identity gives near (200,100,50); World = RotationY(Pi) flips the normal to lit black.
180 degrees, not 90, was chosen because a 90-degree rotation turns the quad edge-on so 'draws nothing' and 'draws black' read back identically; 180 keeps the silhouette and discriminates.

concepts.section: A second, narrower gap this one uncovered, then closed: arbitrary layouts
concepts.text: The first 3D route knew only EasyGL's fixed strides, and a stride does not describe its fields (two 48-byte layouts can differ); ported sample shaders such as normal mapping need other arrangements.
tokens: a stride is not a description

concepts.section: A second, narrower gap this one uncovered, then closed: arbitrary layouts
concepts.text: Every vertex buffer passes its VertexDeclaration to the renderer through the mandatory IVertexBufferRenderer::SetVertexDeclaration, and the GL renderers bind a custom program's attributes by element index; the chapter's 'default no-op' description of that method is stale (it is pure virtual).
concepts.note: Corrected: mandatory, not a default no-op.

concepts.section: A second, narrower gap this one uncovered, then closed: arbitrary layouts
concepts.text: easygl_shadereffect_custom_vertex_layout_test.cpp uses a five-element 48-byte layout and writes vec4(Normal.x, Tangent.y, TexCoord.x, Color.r), drawn twice with independent attribute sets, proving each attribute comes from its own offset.

concepts.section: A second, narrower gap this one uncovered, then closed: arbitrary layouts
concepts.text: The declaration-driven binding is additive: without a declaration the stride-keyed built-in path still applies.
A port that uses only SpriteBatch and the five stock effects runs on CNA's renderer-owned implementations.

A port that loads compiled Effect Framework bytecode needs FNA3D or one of the nine opt-in configurations; .fx/HLSL source, DXBC and MGFX are refused at run time, and .fx can be compiled only at build time through cna-content and an external legacy compiler.
concepts.note: Corrected option count; build-time route added.

concepts.text: A port rewritten to ShaderEffect depends on each renderer's contract: GL text, SPIR-V on Vulkan, WGSL on WebGPU, HLSL on Direct3D, with the 3D coverage listed per renderer.
concepts.note: Updated for WebGPU and 3D coverage at TARGET.

concepts.text: The accurate statement is neither 'compiled effects are unsupported' nor 'every format works everywhere': four separately implemented contracts with separate evidence.
